# `silk/platform/wasm/host`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Random bytes, clocks, and the time zone setting from a JavaScript host, for the providers of
`Random`, `SystemClock`, `MonotonicClock`, and `LocalZone` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

## When to use
Application code does not call it. `OsRandom`, `OsSystemClock`, `OsMonotonicClock`, and
`OsLocalZone` use it when the program runs in a browser, Node.js, Deno or another JavaScript host, so the same
provider works on every target.

## Details
The module imports three host functions from the import module `silk`, and a program imports
only the ones it reads:

| Import | Does |
|---|---|
| `random(address, length)` | Fills `length` bytes at `address` with secure random bytes, as `crypto.getRandomValues` does |
| `clock(monotonic)` | Returns milliseconds as an `f64`: since 1970 when `monotonic` is 0, since a fixed start (`performance.now()`) when it is 1 |
| `time-zone(address, capacity)` | Writes the IANA name of the zone of the host, as `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` gives it, at `address`, and returns its length in bytes, or 0 if the host has no name or it is longer than `capacity` |

The standard library's runner, `host/wasm-runner.mjs`, supplies all three. The `mount` of
`ui-app-dom` supplies `random` and `clock`.

## Gotchas
- A host that instantiates the module itself supplies the imports the module names, or the
  instantiation fails.
- A JavaScript host cannot block, so a wait reads the monotonic clock until the deadline. It
  holds the thread, and in a browser page it holds the page.
- A browser rounds `performance.now()`, often to 5 or 100 microseconds.
